text:
maria: quick follow-up from the micro-arena spike doc i posted earlier — sketching an implementation we could try for NUMA-aware small-allocation fragmentation reduction. idea: per-tenant micro-arenas pinned to a NUMA node, with a decay-based reclaimer that frees cold small slabs back to a shared pool.

aj: can you sketch the life-cycle? how do we decide "cold" vs "hot" for tiny tensor bins?

maria: rough: each micro-arena maintains counters per-size-class. on allocation we bump a hot counter; periodic sampler decays counters. when a class falls below threshold for X seconds, we mark slabs reclaimable and issue an async free to shared staging.

kai: curious about cross-NUMA placement — if tenant's traffic hops nodes, won't we get lots of misses and more fragmentation?

maria: yeah. two levers: (1) prefer local NUMA micro-arena when request originates on that node, (2) allow soft-lease migration: when >Y% of allocations for tenant are from another node for T seconds, start migrating active slabs with a small batch copy. migration is optional and opt-in per tenant.

nora: what about interaction with KV cache and prefix caching? we already have pinned host pages for KV entries, plus kernel pinned staging for evictions. freeing slabs needs coordination.

maria: agree — reclaimer emits events: `reclaim-request` -> offload coordinator attempts to flush or transfer KV entries using that slab first. if coordinator says "in-use" we skip. also we only reclaim slabs with no outstanding kvcache refs.

samir: perf numbers? did you bench this locally?

maria: small synthetic: micro-arena enabled on dev node for 3 tenants. tail p99 latency unchanged, median improved 6% for small token workloads, fragmentation (measured as wasted bytes / total) dropped from ~18% to ~9% after 30m. rough numbers, i can paste logs later.

aj: what about worst-case churn? if we mis-tune decay you could thrash: allocate/free constantly across NUMA nodes. need hysteresis and rate limits.

maria: planned: decay factor out of band-config, and a per-tenant `reclaim-rate-limit` (ops surface). also metric `microarena-thrash` that increments when same page freed+realloc within 10s.

kai: safety: any ABI/allocator contract changes? we need to keep current `free()` semantics.

maria: no ABI changes. micro-arenas are a layered allocator in user space runtime; fall back to global allocator when cross-compat needed. only gating change is an opt-in feature flag. code example below for the runtime config:

```yaml
runtime:
  alloc:
    micro_arena:
      enabled: true
      default_decay_window_s: 120
      reclaim_rate_limit_per_tenant_mb_s: 16
      numa_affinity: prefer_local
      soft_migrate_threshold_pct: 40
```

nora: ops needs a way to opt tenants into canary and a knob to rollback quickly. can we expose per-tenant API & console flag?

maria: yes — control plane adds `tenant.micro_arena: on|off|canary` and a `rollout_group` tag. will push a small control-plane PR.

ops-bot: deploybot: staged rollout plan required before enabling on prod clusters. see /deploy checklist.

aj: how do we measure fragmentation on prod without adding too much overhead? sampling + passive byte accounting maybe.

samir: we have `resident_bytes` per-alloc-class already instrumented in runtime. add `micro_arena_reclaimable_bytes` and expose as a per-tenant gauge. set alerts at 20% wasted.

maria: i'll add those metrics and a small grafana panel mock. also propose an A/B: 10% of traffic for 6h per-region, check p95/p99, fragmentation, OOMs.

kai: does this affect hot restart/startup memory footprint? micro-arenas might warm slower.

maria: startup: we prime micro-arenas lazily. we can seed from previous profile for tenants with historical traces, else start empty. seed is optional via `initial_profile`.

aj: question re: kernel pinned staging pages — freeing them might require unpin+munmap which is expensive. who handles that?

maria: reclaimer does unpin asynchronously on low-load windows. immediate free is only for fully host-backed (non-pinned) slabs. pin/unpin ops are rate-limited.

nora: ops checklist items: feature flag, per-tenant toggle, metric panel, rollback playbook, increase watchdog timeout during canary, run heap-fuzzer for 48h.

maria: thanks — i'll open 2 PRs (runtime + control-plane) and a follow-up RFC with config defaults. expected timeline: prototype -> internal canary in 2 sprints -> region canary 1 sprint after.

devbot: noted: issue created #INF-4227 with label `micro-arena-numa`.

samir: ack. please drop the perf logs and the small script you used for measuring fragmentation.

maria: will do. thanks all :rocket:
